scope.description: Public VerifyLeader authority assurance in a crash-free protocol-v3 cluster with stable voter/nonvoter membership, under transport partitions. A replacement leader and its successful command completion precede the verification call. The old peer has no voter-majority communication or subsequent authority acquisition during the invocation.
assumptions: Distinct permanent ServerIDs and unchanged valid membership during the observed partition
Honest actual Raft workers and request/response transports; dropped routes produce errors, never fabricated success
Independent validated node-local timeouts; no crashes or storage loss in this execution
excluded: Log-commit agreement or full read linearizability proof
Crashes, partial storage writes, user restore and mixed protocol versions
Any liveness guarantee from tool deadlines

properties.reason: Independent applicability, correlated prerequisites and fully observed result comparison

adaptations: A transport wrapper counts successful real AppendEntries returns without modifying requests or responses.
The wrapper declines the optional pipeline with ErrPipelineReplicationNotSupported; ordinary replication is retained.
MockFSM is the repository implementation and is read under its mutex; no FSM mutation is injected.
Nonuniform but individually validated node-local timeouts create a finite observation window while every lease/election worker remains active.
No target source or dependency definitions are changed.

plan_uncertainties: Only protocol v3, fixed three-voter/one-nonvoter membership, crash-free in-memory storage and nonpipelined transport are exercised.
All timeouts bound construction/observation only. An unreached prefix or missing return is unknown, not holds or a liveness finding.
Public verification failure in the no-contact control need not occur at an exact deadline or with an exact error string.
The two executions compare connectivity; their election terms, participants and replies are correlated only within each subtest.
This check does not claim invalid log commitment or a production application read violation.
grounding_unresolved: The result isolates a public contract discrepancy; exact vote-edge causality is supported by source and reply counters, not by instrumentation inside notifyAll.
Different configured node timeouts are intentional and scoped. No conclusion is made about a uniform-timeout deployment.
Raw old/new FSM values demonstrate the application states sampled around this API invocation; no separate externally served read API is executed.
Transport counts do not rule out every already-returned pre-partition reply being scheduled late, so they alone do not prove the exact cause.
